sources: CBDT Notification 45/2026 (30-Mar-2026): AY 2026-27 ITR forms; ITR-1/ITR-4 admit up to two house properties
Finance Act 2025 (new regime slabs, 87A rebate, standard deduction)
Income-tax Act s.87A first proviso (clauses (a) and (b) test TOTAL income) and second proviso (rebate capped at tax computed at s.115BAC(1A) rates)
Finance Act 2026: s.139(1) due date for non-audit assessees with business/professional income moved to 31 August; s.139(5) revised return allowed to the end of the AY subject to the s.234I fee
Income-tax Act s.44AD (Rs 2 crore / Rs 3 crore where cash receipts <= 5%), s.44ADA (Rs 50 lakh / Rs 75 lakh), s.44AE (up to 10 goods carriages)
Income-tax Act s.80CCD(2) as amended by Finance (No.2) Act 2024: 14% of salary for every employer where income is chargeable under s.115BAC(1A)
Finance Act 2025 First Schedule Part I Paragraph A (surcharge bands; 25%/37% exclude 111A/112/112A/dividend income)
Income-tax Act s.111A proviso and s.112A(2) proviso (unexhausted basic exemption set off against listed-equity gains)
Income-tax Act s.288A/288B (rounding of total income and tax payable) and Rule 119A (interest base)

Income-tax Act s.24(b) second proviso (interest on a self-occupied house capped at Rs 2 lakh) and s.115BAC(2)(i); incometax.gov.in new-vs-old regime FAQ: interest on borrowed capital for a self-occupied property is not allowed under the new regime
Income-tax Act s.44AD(1) (deemed profit 8% of turnover, 6% of turnover received through digital modes) and s.44ADA(1) (50% of gross receipts)
Income-tax Act s.80D: preventive health check-up payments up to Rs 5,000 count within the 80D limits

Income-tax Act s.23(2) (up to two self-occupied houses at nil annual value, Finance Act 2019), s.24(a) (30% standard deduction), s.24(b) and its second proviso (Rs 2 lakh on a self-occupied house acquired or built with capital borrowed on or after 1 April 1999 and completed within five years, Rs 30,000 otherwise) and the Explanation on pre-construction interest in five equal instalments
Income-tax Act s.44AE(2): Rs 1,000 per ton of gross vehicle weight per month for a heavy goods vehicle, Rs 7,500 per month for any other goods carriage

Income-tax Act ss.70, 71, 71B, 72, 73, 74 and 80: set-off order between heads, carry forward of house-property loss (8 years), business loss (8), speculative loss (4) and capital loss (8), and the s.80 condition that only a return filed by the s.139(1) due date carries a loss forward (s.71B excepted)

Income-tax Act s.234F (late fee Rs 5,000, or Rs 1,000 where total income does not exceed Rs 5 lakh) and s.234-I as inserted by Finance Act 2026 s.16 with effect from 1 March 2026 (revised return beyond nine months: Rs 1,000 where total income does not exceed Rs 5 lakh, Rs 5,000 otherwise)

Income-tax Act s.44AD(1) and s.44ADA(1) provisos (higher ceiling where cash receipts do not exceed 5% of the total) and s.44AE Explanation (a heavy goods vehicle is one whose gross vehicle weight exceeds 12,000 kg)

deadlineCitations.itr1_2: s.139(1) Explanation 2(c): 31 July for non-audit assessees without business or professional income
deadlineCitations.itr3_4_nonAudit: s.139(1) as amended by Finance Act 2026: 31 August for non-audit assessees with business or professional income (AY 2026-27 onward)
deadlineCitations.audit: s.139(1) Explanation 2(a): 31 October where accounts are audited (audit report due 30 September)
deadlineCitations.belated: s.139(4): 31 December of the AY, or completion of assessment, whichever is earlier
deadlineCitations.revised: s.139(5) as substituted by Finance Act 2026: any time before the end of the AY, subject to the s.234I fee where revised after 31 December

tdsCorrectionWindow.description: Deductor correction statements: 6 years from the end of the FY in which the statement was due (proviso to s.200(3), Finance (No.2) Act 2024), cut to 2 years from 1 April 2026 under s.397(3)(f) of the Income-tax Act 2025
